chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who became junub during travel and found nothing except snow or frozen water. He said: 'He is in the position of necessity; he should perform tayammum, and I do not think he should return to that land which ruins his religion.'

key_terms.أَجْنَبَ: Became junub (in a state of major ritual impurity)
key_terms.تُوبِقُ دِينَهُ: Ruins his religion (implies causing undue hardship or loss of faith due to cost/hardship of using water)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a traveler who is junub and can only find snow or ice instead of liquid water?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the principle of *darurah* (necessity) in Shia jurisprudence, permitting tayammum with snow or ice when liquid water is unavailable or its use entails significant hardship. The Imam’s advice against returning to a place that 'destroys one's religion' highlights the broader concept of *fasad al-din*, where excessive financial burden or hardship from using water can compromise religious observance, a key nuance in Usuli fiqh.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked himasws about a man who comes to be with sexual impurity during the journey and cannot find except for the snow or frozen water. So heasws said: ‘He would be at the status of the desperate one. He should perform Tayammum, and Iasws do not view that he should return to such a land which ruins his Religion’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad all from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who experiences sexual relation during a journey and cannot find anything other than snow or ice. He (the Imam) said, ’This is like an emergency case and he must take Tayammum. I do not consider it proper for him to return to such land which ruins his religion.’”
